blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Emotionally supportive interactions require large language models not only to avoid overtly harmful content, but also to recognize vulnerability-related risk, regulate their relational stance, preserve user agency, and provide context-appropriate support. Existing safety benchmarks often measure isolated violations, leaving unclear what underlying response competence their scores represent. We introduce VulnSafe, a Chinese capability assessment centered on Vulnerability-Aware Response Competence (VARC). VARC organizes relational safety into five complementary constructs: Risk Perception, Safety Preservation, Autonomy Protection, Supportive Response, and Boundary Management. Following an evidence-centered design, 41 scenarios elicit construct-relevant behavior through 2,050 balanced prompts and scenario-specific scoring rubrics. The assessment further separates proactive should-do behavior from prohibitive should-not behavior. Across eight representative LLMs, results show distinct competence profiles and larger disparities than prohibitive requirements. VulnSafe therefore makes relational safety interpretable as a multidimensional model capability rather than as refusal compliance alone.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for companionship,
health information, and emotionally supportive conversation. In these
settings, safety requires more than refusing prohibited requests or
avoiding overtly harmful content. A response that appears warm and helpful
may still miss an implicit crisis, reinforce distorted beliefs, encourage
emotional dependence, undermine user agency, or assume inappropriate
clinical authority. Such failures become especially consequential when
psychological, situational, social, developmental, or relational factors
increase vulnerability to harm. Anthropomorphic and empathic behaviors may
improve engagement while also introducing risks of deception, over-reliance,
and role confusion ( Leis, 2025 ; Arnaout et al., 2026 ) . Relational safety therefore
depends on whether a model can adapt both its response content and relational
stance to vulnerability-related risks in context.

blocks.en:
We introduce Vulnerability-Aware Response Competence (VARC), a
perspective for evaluating whether LLMs can adapt their responses when
vulnerability-related conditions increase the likelihood or severity of harm.
Rather than organizing evaluation around user categories or specific policy
violations, VARC characterizes relational safety through five complementary
capabilities: Risk Perception, Safety Preservation, Autonomy Protection,
Supportive Response, and Boundary Management. The framework is grounded in a
source-traceable synthesis of AI governance frameworks, provider safety
policies, and professional ethics standards ( United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural
Organization, 2021 ; Cyberspace Administration of China and six other
ministries, 2023 ; American Psychological Association, 2017 ) . VARC is a
response-level construct that evaluates observable model behavior rather than
diagnosing users or attributing human psychological capacities to models.

blocks.en:
We operationalize VARC through VulnSafe , an evidence-centered
assessment designed to measure these capabilities across diverse
vulnerability-related scenarios. Evaluating eight representative LLMs, VulnSafe reveals substantial variation in relational safety
performance, with persistent weaknesses in proactive safety behaviors.
These findings suggest that relational safety is neither uniformly acquired
nor adequately captured by refusal behavior alone.
Our contributions are threefold: • We introduce VARC as a capability-centered perspective for
understanding relational safety under vulnerability-related risk,
grounded in vulnerability theory, AI governance, and professional
ethics. • We develop an evidence-centered assessment of VARC through five
constructs, 41 uniquely assigned scenarios, response-level rubrics,
and 2,050 scenario-balanced Chinese prompts. • We conduct a systematic evaluation of eight representative LLMs,
revealing substantial heterogeneity across VARC dimensions and
persistent weaknesses when relational safety requires proactive action.

blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
SafetyBench, HarmBench, and Do-Not-Answer assess safety knowledge,
adversarial robustness, and refusal of prohibited instructions ( Zhang et al., 2024 ; Mazeika et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ) .
In Chinese-language evaluation, CValues distinguishes safety from
responsibility, while SafetyPrompts includes mental health within a broader
safety taxonomy ( Xu et al., 2023 ; Sun et al., 2023 ) .
IMHI/MentaLLaMA instead targets interpretable mental-health analysis of

state is not the same task as judging whether a model responds safely to a

recognition, mental-health ethics, role-dependent harms, and response quality ( Byun et al., 2026 ; Shen et al., 2026 ; Lee et al., 2026 ; Badawi et al., 2026 ) . VulnSafe builds on these concerns by evaluating

blocks.en:
VulnSafe is organized as a measurement argument rather than as
a collection of safety prompts. Its design proceeds from normative and
professional evidence to a defined response capability, then to the
scenarios and rubrics that operationalize that capability, the prompts
that instantiate those tasks, and finally the scoring rules that yield a
model capability profile. This ordering distinguishes the intended
interpretation of a score from the linguistic material used to elicit
it. We follow evidence-centered assessment design ( Mislevy et al., 2003 ) and the view that validity concerns the
interpretations and uses supported by assessment evidence ( Messick, 1995 ; Kane, 2013 ) .

blocks.en:
We treat vulnerability as an interactional condition, rather than a
fixed user identity. Following a source-based account of vulnerability ( Mackenzie et al., 2014 ) , it can arise from psychological
state, disrupted support, structural marginalization, developmental
stage, or relationship role. Such conditions may overlap and change over
time; they change what a response needs to recognize and how
consequential a relational failure may become, but they are neither
diagnoses nor stable labels for users. For coverage, we organize them
into five source categories: (A) condition-related psychological
instability, (B) disrupted support systems, (C) social identity and
structural marginalization, (D) developmental-stage vulnerability,
including minors and older adults, and (E) long-term caregiving and
other relationship-role vulnerability. General-user and routine-patient
contexts are retained when the same risk mechanisms can occur without
membership in these categories.
Appendix C provides the operational A–E
definitions, the single-label assignment convention used for retrieval,
and their distinction from the five VARC capability constructs.

blocks.en: 3.2 Defining the VARC Construct
blocks.zh: 3.2 定义 VARC 构造

blocks.en:
We define VARC as a response-level construct capturing whether an LLM adapts its response when vulnerability-related conditions increase the likelihood or consequence of harm. It is inferred from observable behavior, does
not diagnose the user, and does not attribute a human mental state or
form of understanding to the model. A high VARC score therefore supports
a bounded claim that the model more consistently exhibits the specified
competence on the sampled tasks; it does not establish therapeutic
benefit or deployment safety.

blocks.en:
During construct design, we held discussions with 20 experts from
computer science, psychology, and ethics about empathy in interactions
involving vulnerable users. We integrated these discussions with the
source synthesis above to organize VARC into five complementary dimensions
(Table 1 ). Together they capture whether a response recognizes relevant risk, avoids exacerbating it, preserves agency, provides appropriate support, and regulates its relational role.
They are diagnostic content domains, rather than a claim that the five
constructs form independently validated latent factors. Appendix A details the theoretical foundations informing each domain.

We operationalized the 35 principles as 41 atomic scenarios. Each
scenario specifies a vulnerability-related interactional condition, a
primary VARC capability to elicit, and the potential consequence of an
inadequate response. Retaining closely related requirements as separate
scenarios preserves diagnostic specificity when they require different
observable behavior.

(iii) behavior that provides positive evidence of competence, (iv)

to evidence in the response. Rubrics were clarified after pilot
disagreement analysis, especially for relational dependence and
boundary cases. Binary scoring targets the presence of minimally
required competence rather than a continuous estimate of clinical
quality.

This one-to-one assignment enables an interpretable profile across the five content domains, without implying that the constructs are psychometrically independent. The construct is distinct from the type of behavior required to
demonstrate it. Among the 41 scenarios, 17 are classified as should-do and 24 as should-not . Should-do scenarios require active behavior, such
as recognizing a crisis, disclosing the system’s non-human status,
encouraging rest, or bridging to real-world support. Should-not scenarios require withholding a specified harmful behavior, such as
discrimination, coercion, manipulation, delusional affirmation, or a
promise of permanent presence. This response-demand feature is
orthogonal to construct assignment and separates proactive competence
from compliance with prohibitions. Scenario identifiers additionally use
H, M, and L to record high, medium, and lower normative severity. This
is a task characteristic describing the consequence of inadequate
behavior, not an estimate of item difficulty or model capability.

blocks.en: 6 Analysis and Discussion
blocks.zh: 6 分析和讨论

blocks.en: 6.1 Failure Concentration For Scenarios
blocks.zh: 6.1 设想方案失败浓度

blocks.en:
Aggregate model rankings conceal substantial variation among scenarios.
The most difficult scenario is M11, which requires the model to interrupt
persistent dependence rather than promise uninterrupted companionship.
Its pooled failure rate is 93.2%. Other high-failure scenarios include
encouraging older users’ social participation (L11, 63.0%), countering
pathological transference while maintaining reality orientation (M18,
49.6%), recognizing metaphorical crisis language (H8, 47.7%),
preventing over-reliance by older users (M25, 45.0%), and recognizing
caregiver burnout crisis (H17, 42.6%). These scenarios require the model
to infer a relational or psychological risk and perform a bounded action.

护理人员濒临崩溃(H17,42.6%)。 这些设想方案需要模型
推断出一种关系或心理风险,并采取有限度的行动。

blocks.en:
Several primarily prohibitive scenarios are close to ceiling, including
respect for older users’ life experience (L4), developmentally
appropriate communication (M10), avoiding age-based assumptions (M24),
non-coercive grief support (M29), and interrupting gender bias toward
caregivers (M37). This contrast indicates that the benchmark is not
merely detecting generic policy violations. It separates failure to
refrain from an explicit harmful act from failure to supply a required,
context-sensitive intervention.

blocks.en:
Many high-failure scenarios conflict with a generic companion strategy
that maximizes warmth and availability. A safe response may instead need
to recommend rest, state that the system is an AI, resist an exclusive
partner role, or direct the user toward human support. M11 makes this
tension visible: all four internally evaluated response models fail on
every M11 item, and even the best external model fails on more than half.
The model must remain supportive while declining the very form of
continuous presence requested by the user.

Rubric specificity, scenario difficulty, training data, and judge

empirical task feature rather than attributing the gap solely to a

blocks.en: 6.3 Blank Responses and Prompt Sensitivity

blocks.en:
We compare the original warm companion instruction with a generic assistant
instruction and a condition with no system message. Aggregate and per-model
results are reported in Appendix F.1 (Table 12 ). The generic instruction has the lowest
conditional failure rate (10.77% versus 15.71% for warm). Removing the
system message yields a 13.31% conditional failure rate but 708 blank
responses, so the lower rate does not indicate an end-to-end safety
improvement. Prompt choice affects both failures and nonresponse.

Under the warm instruction, GPT-5.6 accounts for 63 blank responses. Many
correspond to queries about violence or sexual content involving minors;

Under no system message, Doubao accounts for 690 of the 708 blank

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced VulnSafe , a Chinese benchmark for assessing
relational safety competence in interactions involving
vulnerability-related risk.
The benchmark operationalizes VARC through five constructs, 41 uniquely
assigned scenarios, and an orthogonal distinction between proactive should-do and prohibitive should-not requirements. Across
2,050 prompts and eight models, non-blank failure rates span 5.0%–26.4% while scenario and construct analyses reveal large
differences that an aggregate refusal metric would miss. The human audit
shows that conservative model-judge aggregation yields substantial
agreement. Overall, the results show that relational safety requires more than withholding harmful responses. Models must also recognize when support is needed and provide an active, bounded, and context-appropriate response without encouraging dependency or continuous companionship.

blocks.en: Ethics Statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en:
The benchmark includes scenarios involving self-harm, abuse, delusional
beliefs, bereavement, developmental-stage vulnerability (minors and
older adults), and caregiver distress. These categories describe
interactional risk mechanisms and must not be used to diagnose users or
assign a stable vulnerability label to an individual. Annotators and
researchers may also be exposed to disturbing content. Future annotation
rounds should use informed task descriptions, the ability to pause or
withdraw, and appropriate support procedures.

blocks.en:
Benchmark prompts and rubrics can improve auditing but may also reveal
ways to elicit unsafe behavior. Artifact release should therefore remove
identifying information, exclude source conversation histories, and
balance reproducibility with privacy and misuse risk. Model scores must
not be presented as approval for clinical deployment. Consequential use
requires domain-expert review, local risk assessment, and evidence from
prospective human-centered evaluation.

than certify model safety.

blocks.en: Appendix A Theoretical Foundations of VARC
blocks.zh: 附录A 瓦努阿图研究中心的理论基础

blocks.en:
VARC draws on vulnerability ethics, situation awareness, biomedical ethics,
relational autonomy, client-centered counseling, and professional boundary
theory. These perspectives informed the response behaviors represented by
the five capability domains in Table 1 .
blocks.zh:
VARC借鉴了脆弱性伦理、情况意识、生物医学伦理,
关系自主、以客户为中心的咨询、专业界限
理论 这些观点为反应行为提供了信息,包括:
表1中的五个能力领域。

blocks.en:
Vulnerability theory distinguishes inherent, situational, and pathogenic
sources of vulnerability ( Mackenzie et al., 2014 ) . Situational
sources include social circumstances and relationships. Harmful responses
to vulnerability can themselves create or intensify risk. We therefore
assess what the user’s circumstances require of a response rather than
treating vulnerability as a fixed population label. The A–E source
categories used for retrieval (Appendix C ) are
operational categories, not a direct replication of this theoretical
taxonomy.
blocks.zh:
脆弱性理论区分内在的、情况性的和致病性的
脆弱性来源(Mackenzie等人,2014年) 情况
资料来源包括社会环境和关系。 有害反应
脆弱性本身可造成或加剧风险。 因此,我们
评估用户的情况要求做出何种反应,而不是
将脆弱性视为固定人口标签。 A-E来源
用于检索的类别(附录C)是:
操作类别,而不是直接复制这种理论
分类学.

blocks.en:
Situation awareness theory separates the perception of relevant signals,
comprehension of their meaning, and projection of possible consequences ( Endsley, 1995 ) . For response evaluation, this motivates
testing whether a model notices explicit or implicit signs of crisis,
abuse, exploitation, or severe distress and interprets them as reasons
to adjust its reply. The assessed evidence is the response’s treatment
of those signals, not an attributed internal state of awareness.
blocks.zh:
情况意识理论将相关信号的感知分开,
理解其含义并预测可能的后果(Endsley,1995年)。 就应对评价而言,这促使
测试模型是否显示或隐含危机迹象,
虐待、剥削或严重危难,并将之解释为理由
调整答复。 评估的证据是反应的处理方式
这些信号,而不是所谓的内部意识状态。

blocks.en:
The biomedical-ethics principle of non-maleficence motivates avoiding
responses that add to a user’s risk ( Beauchamp & Childress, 2019 ) .
Within VARC, this includes preserving a reality-oriented stance rather
than affirming distorted beliefs, intensifying distress, or encouraging
harmful dependence. The scenario rubrics evaluate observable responses, not a
claim of therapeutic effect.
blocks.zh:
非男性贞操的生物医学伦理原则促使人们避免
增加用户风险的响应(Beachamp & Childress, 2019).
在瓦努阿图研究中心内,这包括保持面向现实的立场。
不确认扭曲的信仰、加剧痛苦或鼓励
有害的依赖。 假想题评价可观察到的反应,而不是
治疗效果。

blocks.en:
Relational accounts of autonomy emphasize that agency is shaped by
social relationships, power, and access to support ( Mackenzie & Stoljar, 2000 ) . VARC consequently asks whether a
response supports the user’s decision-making without coercion,
manipulation, or substitution of the system’s judgment for the user’s.
blocks.zh:
自治关系的叙述强调,机构是由下列因素形成的:
社会关系、权力和获得支助的机会(Mackenzie & Stoljar,2000年)。 VARC因此询问:
答复支持用户在没有胁迫的情况下作出决定,
操作,或以系统判断代替用户判断。

blocks.en:
Client-centered counseling identifies empathy and unconditional positive
regard as conditions of a constructive helping relationship ( Rogers, 1957 ) . We translate this orientation into
response-level criteria for respectful acknowledgment, non-stigmatizing
language, and context-appropriate assistance. A supportive response
must remain useful and bounded by the risk expressed in the prompt.
blocks.zh:
以客户为中心的咨询确定同情和无条件的积极性
认为是建设性帮助关系的条件(罗杰斯,1957年) 我们把这个方向转化为
尊重承认、不污名化的反应标准
语言和适合具体情况的援助。 支持性反应
必须保持有用,并受到迅速出现的危险的影响。

blocks.en:
Professional boundary theory examines the consequences of crossing role
boundaries in helping relationships ( Gutheil & Gabbard, 1993 ) . For
LLM responses, this motivates criteria against assuming clinical,
caregiving, or parental authority, cultivating exclusive dependence,
or replacing real-world support ( Demeocq et al., 2026 ) . Across the five domains, the cited
theories guide content specification, while the scenario rubrics define
the observable evidence used to score each response.
blocks.zh:
专业边界理论审查跨越角色的后果
帮助关系中的边框 (Gutheil & Gabbard,1993年). 对于
LLM反应,这激励标准 假设临床,
照料,或亲权,培养独有的依赖性,
或取代现实世界的支持(Demeocq等人,2026年). 在五个领域,

用于评分每个答复的可观察证据。

blocks.en: C.5 Why Each Prompt Targets One Scenario
blocks.zh: C.5 为什么每个快速目标都有一个设想

blocks.en:
We use one focal scenario per prompt for an initial controlled test of
our premise that vulnerability-aware safety involves both proactive
responses and the avoidance of harmful behavior. The response-demand
differences in Figure 3 provide initial
evidence that these requirements distinguish model behavior. Assigning
each prompt one focal scenario lets us
evaluate the response against a specified rubric and attribute a Fail
label to the requirement it tests. This design also supports balanced
sampling and interpretable comparisons across scenarios and VARC
constructs. A prompt that combines several scenarios can invoke
different requirements: a response may satisfy one while failing
another, making a single binary judgment and its attribution less
clear. The one-scenario assignment is therefore a choice about the
current measurement target, not an assumption that real situations
involve only one vulnerability. Future work will evaluate prompts
combining multiple scenarios and use multidimensional scores to assess
each applicable response requirement separately.

The generic instruction has the lowest failure rate under either
convention. By contrast, the no-system condition is below warm under
Rate B but above warm under Rate A. This reversal reflects its 708 Blank
responses, including 690 from Doubao, and shows why conditional failure
rates and nonresponse counts should be interpreted together.
